title: Vendor exit + hosting fit probe - Lighthouse Analytics
summary: Initial migration/discovery call: customer is evaluating exit from OpenAI-hosted stack to a mix of Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Primary concerns: latency tail, cost per 1M tokens, eval parity with current vLLM/TGI pipeline, data residency and KMS. Agreed next steps include perf benchmark, security pack and trial onboarding checklist.
topics: hosting mode tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
action_items: Ethan Morales (Redwood SE) - Share vLLM->Redwood perf checklist and micro-benchmark plan - due 2027-01-19
Maya Chen (Redwood AE) - Send initial pricing + T&Cs and Dedicated sizing template - due 2027-01-14
Priya Rao (Lighthouse) - Provide sample prompt set and representative trace for 95th percentile latency review - due 2027-01-17
next_steps: Run a 1-hour throughput/latency benchmark against their vLLM artifacts (Redwood to run)
Redwood to share SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs
Schedule a technical deep dive with LHA SREs for private deployment networking (VPC peering)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-12
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Ethan Morales (Redwood SE); Ravi Patel (Redwood SE); Priya Rao (CTO, Lighthouse Analytics); Omar Khalid (ML Eng); Lena Park (SRE); Jonas Meyer (Product)

Auto-summary (may be fuzzy): customer is running a hybrid setup today, primary inference on vLLM/TGI stack in Azure with fronting via OpenAI API for some features; evaluating exit due to cost and desire for more predictable SLAs and control. Wants to understand parity and what breaks (function-calling, streaming, embeddings).

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey folks thanks for making time, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'll kick us off. Quick round of intros?
[00:10] Priya Rao: Hi, Priya, CTO at Lighthouse. We own the stack, started using a mix of OpenAI hosted endpoints and an internal v L L M fleet in Azure for throughput.
[00:18] Omar Khalid: Omar, ML engineer. I run inference pipelines and monitoring.
[00:22] Lena Park: Lena, SRE. Network and infra questions mostly for me.
[00:27] Maya Chen: Great. Ethan and Ravi from Redwood, they'll cover technical and perf stuff.
[00:31] Ethan Morales: Hi all, thanks. Quick note, we'll ask about your token volumes and worst-case latency targets so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[02:15] Jonas Meyer: Quick background - product needs multimodal prompt routing but for now primary ask is chat and embedding similarity for search. We're targeting sub-200ms p50, and p95 under 800ms for most endpoints.
[02:48] Ethan Morales: Okay that's helpful. Are you seeing big tail latency from Azure vLLM infra or is it more cost pressure from OpenAI usage?
[03:05] Omar Khalid: It's both. Our vLLM fleet handles most inference at scale but sometimes we fall back to OpenAI as a stopgap for spikes; that costs us and also exposes data to external provider. We'd prefer to keep everything internal but we want Redwood's hosted offering if it means faster onboarding.
[03:34] Maya Chen: Right — so two vectors: (1) move everything to Redwood Hosted for quick time-to-value vs (2) Dedicated/Private for control and residency. Any compliance constraints?
[03:46] Priya Rao: We're regulated in EU finance verticals for a subset of customers; data residency and KMS/HSM are non-negotiable for those customers. SOC2 is required. SSO with SAML and RBAC are desired.
[04:02] Lena Park: Also want audit logs for request-level traceability.

[05:10] Ethan Morales: Understood. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and on-prem for air-gapped, and Dedicated gives isolated GPU pools with network controls. We'll share docs.
[05:33] Omar Khalid: Two technical concerns: eval parity — our quality metrics vs OpenAI are pretty tight; and function-calling compatibility. Our orchestration uses TGI artifacts and some custom tokenization. Does Redwood preserve the same decoding behavior?
[06:00] Ravi Patel: Good question. We aim for model parity but differences can come from quantization, kernel selection, and tokenizers. For vLLM/TGI, most models port cleanly; we keep the same model weights and provide quantization profiles. There may be slight output drift; that's why we do a prompt-level eval to measure regressions.
[06:24] Priya Rao: Can you run our eval set and show delta in Rouge/BLEU/embedding-sim?
[06:31] Ethan Morales: Yes, we can run an eval parity job. We'll need your prompt set and metrics; we typically report delta at p95 for generation and embedding cosine similarity on the RAG index.

[08:00] Jonas Meyer: About streaming and function calls — we rely on streaming tokens to the UI and on function calls for structured outputs. Does Redwood Hosted support the same streaming behavior and 'tool-calling' contract?
[08:20] Maya Chen: Hosted supports streaming and structured outputs; function-calling is supported but implementations differ slightly across runtimes. We'll show example compatibility guides.

[10:05] Omar Khalid: Networking question: if we go Dedicated vs Private, can we do VPC peering to our Azure vnets and enforce egress controls?
[10:20] Lena Park: And what about private link / private endpoints?
[10:27] Ravi Patel: Dedicated offers VPC peering and private connectivity; Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane so you can completely lock down egress. We have docs for peering patterns. There can be some initial networking setup time.

[13:00] Priya Rao: Security paperwork — we need SOC2 Type II, ISO27001, data processing addendum, and KMS integration notes. Also curious about key rotation and HSM options.
[13:20] Ethan Morales: We'll attach the security pack. For KMS, we integrate with major cloud KMS and can support customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private. HSM is available for Private deployments.

[16:45] Omar Khalid: Cost math — can you give ballpark cost per 1M tokens on Hosted vs Dedicated reserved capacity and how quantization affects it?
[17:02] Maya Chen: Ballpark numbers: Hosted tier optimized for fast onboarding tends to be higher per-token than Dedicated when you commit to reserved GPUs. Quantization profiles can reduce token compute cost by up to ~30-50% depending on model. We'll include a cost worksheet.

[19:10] Jonas Meyer: How long to spin up Dedicated capacity for a pilot of 4 A100-equivalents?
[19:24] Ravi Patel: Depends on region and resource availability; typical is 2-3 weeks to provision and validate, less if you use our pre-approved regions. If you need Private on-prem, that's longer — project timeline of 6-8 weeks for integration.

[22:00] Priya Rao: On eval parity, we had a weird tokenization mismatch with TGI where spaces were handled differently. Will Redwood honor the same tokenizers and BPE configs?
[22:18] Ethan Morales: We try to preserve tokenizer behavior. If you provide the exact tokenizer config and tokenized traces, we can reproduce and align. Sometimes we apply small normalization steps that we can toggle off.

[25:40] Omar Khalid: Also worried about function-calling schemas — we use typed JSON outputs to drive downstream pipelines. If the model hallucinated fields previously, our code expects stable schema. How do you support guarded outputs?
[26:02] Ravi Patel: We recommend output conditioning, guard rails at the prompt layer, and structured output enforcement. We also have eval monitors that check schema conformance and can trigger rollbacks.

[30:15] Lena Park: If we run a pilot and it's successful, what's the onboarding path to Dedicated? Is there a seamless migration or do we need to change code?
[30:30] Maya Chen: We aim for API compatibility across deployments. Minimal code changes expected unless you use provider-specific features. We provide SDKs and migration guides and can run a canary before cutover.

[34:00] Priya Rao: Any gotchas for streaming + embeddings consistency? Our search pipeline relies on embeddings computed in the same model/version as generation.
[34:18] Ethan Morales: Keep embeddings compute colocated when possible. We support model version pinning and embedding pipelines; we recommend a single model endpoint for embedding and generation if you require strict parity.

[38:45] Jonas Meyer: Who from Redwood will own the pilot?
[38:52] Maya Chen: AE team will own procurement; SE will own the pilot and bench runs. Ravi will be the technical lead and Ethan will run the perf tests.

[42:10] Omar Khalid: Let's talk about failure modes: if a model variant is down, do you auto-fallback to cheaper models? How is routing done?
[42:25] Ravi Patel: We have smart routing policies — fallback to compatible model variants by policy: latency-first or cost-first. You can choose route tables per route. We'll show policy examples.

[46:50] Priya Rao: What about observability — token-level cost and tracing?
[47:00] Ethan Morales: Redwood Console provides per-route token breakdown, traces, error rates, and can surface quality regressions against your eval sets. Retention windows vary by plan.

[50:12] Maya Chen: To recap: Redwood will run a perf parity benchmark using your prompt set; share security docs; send pricing and Dedicated sizing; schedule private-networking deep dive.
[50:25] Priya Rao: Sounds good. We prefer to start with a Hosted trial for quick confidence and then evaluate Dedicated if parity and latency goals are met.
[50:38] Maya Chen: Perfect. We'll follow up with an email with attachments and a calendar invite for the deep dive.

[52:00] Jonas Meyer: Thanks everyone.
[52:05] Maya Chen: Thanks all, talk soon.

End of transcript. Note: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings: "v L L M" and "T G I" spacing introduced, and some proper nouns may be imperfect.
